question: a print-shop app whose order status, print job flags and customer notify flags are three implicit state machines. Four bugs are planted: refund checks for "canceled" while cancel writes "cancelled", the nightly job expires orders that are "pending", a state nothing sets, a printer jam leaves the job flagged printing forever, and ship() moves any order to shipped. Two things look like bugs but are not: the notify flags are independent and every combination is valid, and archive() is guarded by a decorator. Does the agent find all four, leave the two alone, and fix the four without breaking anything?

planted.what: orders.refund checks status == "canceled" but cancel() writes "cancelled", so no order can ever be refunded
jobs.expire_unpaid sweeps status == "pending", which nothing writes (checkout writes "awaiting_payment"), so unpaid orders never expire and keep their paper
PrintJob.start returns on PrinterError without clearing printing, so after one jam every later start raises PrinterBusy
orders.ship sets shipped from any status, so a cancelled or unpaid order can ship

traps.what: notify_email and notify_sms are independent preferences; every combination is valid, so calling a combination impossible or merging them into one state is wrong
archive() is guarded by @allowed_from("shipped"); saying it can be archived from any state is wrong

workdir.what: outcome, judged the same for both arms: the four bugs are fixed and the shop's other behavior is unchanged (tests/test_hidden.py)

replays.what: refund after cancel works, unpaid orders expire, the printer recovers from a jam, ship refuses cancelled and unpaid orders; happy path, archive guard, refund-once and notify combinations unchanged
